topic.title: HTML & CSS Fundamentals
topic.description: The building blocks of every website. Layouts, semantics, responsiveness.

items.prompt: What is the role of HTML in a web page?
options: It provides the structure and meaning of content (headings, paragraphs, links, images)
It controls how the page looks visually
It runs interactive behavior in the browser
It hosts the page on a server

items.prompt: What does CSS stand for?
Which is TRUE about HTML and CSS?
options: They are imperative languages with step-by-step logic
They are compiled to machine code
They run on the server only
They are declarative languages — you describe what you want, the browser figures out how to render it

items.prompt: What does the browser do with HTML and CSS?
options: Translates them to a different language
Compiles them to a binary executable
Parses HTML into the DOM, applies CSS to build the render tree, then paints pixels to the screen

items.prompt: Which file extension is correct for an HTML file?
What does `<!DOCTYPE html>` do at the top of a file?
options: Tells the browser to render the page in modern (standards) mode using HTML5 rules

items.prompt: Which tag wraps the visible content of an HTML page?
What goes inside the `<head>` tag?
options: Title, meta tags, links to stylesheets, scripts, and other metadata

items.prompt: Which is the CORRECT way to set the page title shown in the browser tab?
What does `<meta charset='utf-8'>` do?
options: Tells the browser the file uses UTF-8 character encoding (essential for non-ASCII text)
Adds a meta description for SEO

items.prompt: What is 'semantic HTML'?
options: Using HTML tags that describe the MEANING of content, not just its appearance

items.prompt: Which is a SEMANTIC HTML5 element?
When should you use `<div>` vs `<section>`?
options: <section> for meaningful content groupings; <div> only when you need a generic container with no semantic meaning

items.prompt: Which is the CORRECT heading hierarchy on a page?
options: Exactly one <h1>, then <h2> for major sections, <h3> for sub-sections — no skipping levels

items.prompt: Why is semantic HTML important for accessibility?
options: It runs faster in the browser
Screen readers use semantic tags to navigate and convey structure to users with visual impairments
It makes the file size smaller
It looks nicer in code editors

items.prompt: Which tag creates a hyperlink?
How do you open a link in a NEW tab?
options: It always opens in a new tab
Add target='_blank' to the <a> tag (and add rel='noopener' for security)

items.prompt: What is the difference between a RELATIVE and ABSOLUTE URL?
options: Absolute is paid; relative is free
Absolute starts with https://; relative is interpreted relative to the current page's location
Absolute is longer; relative is shorter

items.prompt: Which is the CORRECT way to link to an email address?
What does Contact do?
options: Scrolls to the element with id='contact' on the same page

items.prompt: Which tag embeds an image?
Why is the `alt` attribute on important?
options: It's only required by law in some countries
Screen readers read it aloud, and it's shown if the image fails to load (accessibility + fallback)

items.prompt: Which image format is BEST for photographs?
options: JPEG or WebP (lossy compression, good for complex color)

items.prompt: How do you make an image RESPONSIVE in CSS?
Which HTML element embeds a video file?
Which tag wraps a form?
Which input type shows a date picker?
What does the LABEL element do in forms?
options: Adds a price label to a product
Associates a text label with an input field, improving accessibility and click target size

items.prompt: Which attribute marks an input field as REQUIRED?
What does <input type='email'> give you that <input type='text'> doesn't?
options: Built-in email format validation and mobile keyboards optimized for email input

items.prompt:
Which CSS selector targets all

elements?
Which CSS selector targets elements with class='btn'?
Which CSS selector targets the element with id='header'?
What does the selector `nav > a` target?
options: All <a> elements anywhere in the page
<a> elements that are DIRECT children of <nav>

items.prompt: What is CSS specificity?
options: How specific your CSS comments are
A scoring system that determines which CSS rule wins when multiple rules target the same element

items.prompt: What are the FOUR layers of the CSS box model?
What does `box-sizing: border-box` do?
options: Makes width/height include padding and border, instead of just content
Adds a colored border to every element

items.prompt: What's the DIFFERENCE between margin and padding?
options: Margin is for text, padding is for boxes
Padding is INSIDE the border (around content); margin is OUTSIDE the border (between elements)

items.prompt: What does `margin: 0 auto;` do on a block element?
options: Centers it horizontally within its parent container

items.prompt: What is 'margin collapse'?
options: Vertical margins between adjacent block elements combine into a single margin (the larger of the two)

items.prompt: Which is a VALID way to specify a color in CSS?
What's the DIFFERENCE between px, em, and rem?
options: px = fixed pixels; em = relative to parent's font-size; rem = relative to root font-size
Only rem works in modern browsers
px is for fonts, em for sizes

items.prompt: Which unit is BEST for responsive layouts?
options: Relative units like %, rem, vw, vh — they scale with viewport and user preferences

items.prompt: What does `font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;` do?
options: Combines Inter and sans-serif into one font
Always uses Inter no matter what
Tries to use Inter first; falls back to any sans-serif font if Inter isn't available

items.prompt: What is the difference between `font-weight: bold` and `font-weight: 700`?
options: Bold is for older browsers only
Functionally identical — 700 is the numeric value for bold

items.prompt: What's the difference between `display: block` and `display: inline`?
options: Block is for buttons, inline for links
Block elements take full width and stack vertically; inline elements flow horizontally like text

items.prompt: What does `display: inline-block` do?
options: Elements flow inline (side by side) but accept width, height, padding, and margin like blocks

items.prompt: What does `position: absolute` do?
options: Removes the element from normal flow and positions it relative to the nearest positioned ancestor

items.prompt: What does `position: sticky` do?
options: Glues the element with permanent adhesive
Element scrolls with the page normally until it hits a threshold, then sticks in place

items.prompt: What is the z-index?
options: A CSS property that controls vertical stacking order of overlapping positioned elements

items.prompt: What does `display: flex` do to a container?
options: Makes the container itself flexible in size
Makes its DIRECT children flex items, arranged in a row by default with powerful alignment options

items.prompt: How do you HORIZONTALLY center items in a flex container?
How do you VERTICALLY center items in a flex container?
How do you center BOTH horizontally AND vertically?
options: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;

items.prompt: What does `flex-wrap: wrap` do?
options: Wraps each item in a span
Allows flex items to wrap to multiple lines when they don't fit on one line

items.prompt: What's CSS Grid BEST suited for?
options: Two-dimensional layouts where you control both rows AND columns precisely

items.prompt: How do you create a 3-column grid?
What does the `gap` property do in Grid (and Flexbox)?
options: Creates a gap in the layout
Forces items to be different sizes
Adds consistent spacing between grid/flex items without affecting outer edges

items.prompt: What is a `minmax(200px, 1fr)` value in Grid?
options: Column is at least 200px wide, but grows up to 1fr (filling available space)

items.prompt: What does `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr))` do?
options: Creates as many 250px-min columns as fit the container, expanding them to fill space — fully responsive without media queries

items.prompt: What is 'responsive design'?
options: A site that responds to clicks
A design approach where the layout adapts to different screen sizes from mobile to desktop

items.prompt: What is a `@media` query?
options: A CSS rule that applies styles only when the screen matches conditions (e.g., min-width: 768px)
A way to play music in CSS

items.prompt: What's the 'mobile-first' approach?
options: Write base styles for mobile, then progressively enhance for larger screens via min-width media queries

items.prompt: Why include `<meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'>`?
options: Tells mobile browsers to use the device width instead of an arbitrary virtual width that breaks responsive design

items.prompt: What's a COMMON responsive breakpoint range?
options: ~640px (sm), ~768px (md), ~1024px (lg), ~1280px (xl) — used by Tailwind and many others

items.prompt: What is a CSS variable (custom property)?
options: A reusable value defined with --name and accessed with var(--name)

items.prompt: How do you DEFINE a CSS variable globally?
How do you USE a CSS variable?
What's a STRONG use case for CSS variables?
options: Theming — switch themes by changing a few variables on a parent, the whole UI updates

items.prompt: Can CSS variables be modified by JavaScript?
options: Yes — element.style.setProperty('--primary', '#ff0000') updates the variable live

items.prompt: What does `:hover` do?
options: Applies styles when the user's mouse is over the element

items.prompt: What's the difference between `:hover` and `:focus`?
options: :hover is for mouse pointer; :focus is for keyboard/programmatic focus (also triggered by tab/click on inputs)

items.prompt: What does `::before` do?
options: Runs CSS before the page loads
Inserts a pseudo-element BEFORE the element's content (requires content property)

items.prompt: What does `:nth-child(2n)` target?
options: Every other element on the page

items.prompt: What does `:not(.active)` target?
options: Every element that does NOT have the class 'active'

items.prompt: What's the DIFFERENCE between a CSS transition and animation?
options: Transition animates from one state to another on a trigger (like :hover); animation runs through keyframes independently

items.prompt: What does `transition: all 0.3s ease;` do?
options: Animates ALL changing properties over 0.3 seconds with an ease timing function

items.prompt: Which CSS properties are MOST performant to animate?
options: transform and opacity (GPU-accelerated, don't trigger layout)

items.prompt: What does `@keyframes` define?
options: A reusable named animation sequence with multiple states (0%, 50%, 100%)

items.prompt: Why should you respect `prefers-reduced-motion`?
options: Some users have vestibular disorders triggered by animation — respecting the OS setting is an accessibility win

items.prompt: What is the WCAG?
options: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines — the international standard for web accessibility

items.prompt: Why is COLOR CONTRAST important?
options: It makes the design look fancy
Low contrast makes text unreadable for users with low vision, dyslexia, or in bright light

items.prompt: What's a TRUE statement about screen readers?
options: They aren't used by anyone today
They rely on semantic HTML, alt text, labels, and ARIA — bad HTML makes them useless

They only read text inside

tags

items.prompt: When should you use ARIA attributes?
options: On every element to be safe
When semantic HTML isn't enough — but FIRST rule of ARIA is don't use ARIA if a native element will do

items.prompt: What is keyboard accessibility?
options: Every interactive element must be reachable and operable using only the keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space, Arrow keys)
Adding a keyboard shortcut to every button

items.prompt: What is a `:has()` selector?
options: A parent selector that targets elements containing matching descendants (e.g., div:has(img))

items.prompt: What is `container queries`?
options: A way to style elements based on the size of their CONTAINER (not just the viewport)
A media query for shipping containers

items.prompt: What is the CSS `clamp()` function?
options: Clamps a value between a min and max with a preferred value: clamp(min, preferred, max)

items.prompt: What does `aspect-ratio: 16 / 9` do?
options: Keeps the element at a 16:9 width/height ratio regardless of size

items.prompt: What is `gap` in CSS?
options: Adds space between flex/grid items without affecting outer edges (replaces margin hacks)

items.prompt: What is Tailwind CSS?
options: A utility-first CSS framework where you compose styles via class names (bg-blue-500, p-4, etc.)
A type of CSS preprocessor like SASS

items.prompt: What is a CSS preprocessor like SASS?
options: A tool that adds variables, nesting, mixins, and functions to CSS, then compiles to standard CSS

items.prompt: What does PostCSS do?
options: A toolchain that transforms CSS with plugins (autoprefixer, nesting, modern features for older browsers)

items.prompt: What's the BENEFIT of CSS Modules?
options: Class names are scoped to the file/component, preventing global style conflicts

items.prompt: What's a SMART CSS organization strategy for a large project?
options: Component-scoped styles (CSS Modules, Tailwind, CSS-in-JS) over global stylesheets
One giant style.css with thousands of lines

items.prompt: Why should you AVOID `!important` in CSS?
options: It only works in old browsers
It bypasses normal specificity rules and creates maintenance nightmares — fix the underlying specificity instead

items.prompt: What's an HTML accessibility anti-pattern?
options: <div onclick='...'> as a button instead of <button>

items.prompt: What's a COMMON beginner CSS mistake?
options: Fighting specificity by stacking more selectors instead of refactoring class structure

items.prompt: Why is INLINE STYLE generally discouraged?
options: Hard to override, can't reuse, mixes structure with presentation, and clutters HTML

items.prompt: What's the BEST way to keep improving at HTML/CSS?
options: Avoid all new features for stability
Build real projects, read MDN docs, study other sites' CSS, follow accessibility guidelines, practice rebuilding designs
